title.rendered: Rising Before Daylight | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 1

excerpt.rendered: Capernaum had been the busiest day of Jesus’ public ministry. Before daylight, He was gone to a solitary place to pray. His public authority flowed from private communion.

content.rendered:
Capernaum had been the busiest day of Jesus’ public ministry so far. He had taught in the synagogue, cast out a demon, healed Peter’s mother-in-law, and stayed up late healing the sick who were brought to Peter’s door. Then, before daylight, Mark tells us Jesus did something that defined the rhythm of every public day that followed.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, October 3, 2026 | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 1

Today’s Scripture

“Now in the morning, having risen a long while before daylight, He went out and departed to a solitary place; and there He prayed.”
Mark 1:35 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

It was the morning after the busiest day of Jesus’ public ministry so far. Mark 1 tells us the whole city of Capernaum had gathered at Peter’s door the night before. Jesus had taught in the synagogue with such authority that the crowds were astonished. He had cast a demon out of a tormented man. He had healed Peter’s mother-in-law of a dangerous fever. Then He had spent the entire evening healing the sick and casting out demons as the crowds pressed in. By the time the house fell silent, it was late. And yet, Mark tells us, before daylight the next morning, Jesus was already up, out of the house, and gone to a solitary place to pray.

This is one of the most instructive sentences in the Gospels for anyone who wants to pray as Jesus prayed. Before the next day’s crowd arrived at the door, Jesus was already in the presence of the Father. His public authority — the authority that commanded demons out of men, healed the sick with a word, calmed the Sea of Galilee, raised the dead — flowed from private communion that happened in the dark, in a solitary place, long before the sun came up. The pattern was not accidental. Luke 5:16 tells us plainly: “So He Himself often withdrew into the wilderness and prayed.”

The Passion Translation renders Mark 1:35 with striking tenderness: “The next morning, Jesus got up long before daybreak and went out alone into the wilderness to pray in solitude” (Mark 1:35 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “And in the morning, long before daylight, He got up and went out to a [deserted] place, and there He prayed” (Mark 1:35 AMPC). Deserted. Solitary. Alone with the Father. Not alone in the lonely sense. Alone in the undistracted sense. One Face. One Voice. One listening Heart.

How Jesus Prayed

The Format. Private. Early. Solitary. Jesus did not pray in Mark 1:35 as a public performance for anyone to see. He stripped away every audience, every distraction, every voice except the Father’s. The format itself preached a sermon. The believer’s deepest prayer life is not for the crowd. It is for the Father in secret.

The Essence. Receive before give. Jesus had given all day to the crowds of Capernaum. By morning He needed to receive again from the Father before another day of giving began. Private communion is where the believer is refilled. The one who tries to give to the world without first receiving from the Father is pouring out of an empty vessel.

The Authority. Every miracle Jesus performed in public flowed from the authority He cultivated in private. The command to the demon came from the time with the Father. The healing of the leper came from the time with the Father. The raising of the dead came from the time with the Father. The authority of the believer in the world is directly proportional to the time the believer spends alone with God.

The Assurance. Jesus came out of the solitary place settled. The disciples found Him and said, “Everyone is looking for You.” He answered without hesitation: “Let us go into the next towns, that I may preach there also, because for this purpose I have come forth.” He knew what He was there for. The time with the Father had given Him clarity. There was no second-guessing.

The Submission. Private prayer is where the believer’s own agenda gets surrendered to the Father’s agenda. Jesus did not go back to Capernaum because the crowd was asking for Him. He went to the next towns because the Father was sending Him. Private prayer is the forge in which the believer’s will is daily aligned with heaven’s.

The Result. A day of ministry marked by clarity, authority, and divine direction. For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, this is the foundation of everything else in this fourteen-day series. If you want to pray as Jesus prayed, begin where He began. In the solitary place. Before daylight. Alone with the Father. The authority you walk in publicly tomorrow will be the authority you cultivated privately today.

Prayer (Pattern After Jesus)

Address. Father, I come to You in the quiet, before the noise of the day begins. I come as a child, not as a performer. I come to receive before I give.

Receive. Speak to me today, Father. Fill me with Your Spirit. Give me clarity for the hours ahead. Show me what You are doing, and let me walk in it.

Submission. Not my agenda today, Father, but Yours. Send me where You are sending me. Keep me from where You are not. Let Your purpose be accomplished through this day of my life.

In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

My public authority flows from private communion with the Father. I pray as Jesus prayed. In the solitary place. Before daylight. Alone with the Father. And I walk out into my day settled, clear, and authorised.
